raw_text:
The objective of this research is to investigate why repeated responses to the same open question can differ while accounting for observable variation. By considering different explanatory factors, this study aims to distinguish between competing theories.

Assumptions
- The participant's experience uniquely contributes to the interpretation of a response.
- Variation in response can be attributed to observable factors.

Research design
A mixed-methods approach is used. Quantitative data through surveys will be collected, while qualitative data through interviews will supplement the findings.

Data or evidence needed
- Surveys asking for responses to the same open question repeatedly.
- Interviews to gather further insight into the participant's responses.

Measurement
- Use same open question and format across all surveys.
- Scale for analyzing quantitative responses (e.g., frequency, intensity).
- Interview transcriptions for qualitative analysis.

Analysis
- Quantitative analysis using statistical tools to identify patterns and correlations.
- Qualitative analysis comparing responses across interviews to detect changes and meanings.

Decision / stopping rule
The study will end after collecting data from a pre-defined sample size with 80% statistical power.

Limitations
- Open-ended responses are subjective and can vary greatly between individuals.
- Observations might be influenced by subtle factors not accounted for.
